title: 2018 年全国硕士研究生招生考试 英语（二）

sections.title: Section I　完形填空
sections.dir: Read the following text. Choose the best word(s) for each numbered blank and mark A, B, C or D. (10 points)
sections.note: 20 题 × 0.5 分。先通读抓主线：本文讲"好奇心为何让人自找痛苦、又该如何自控"。

paras.en: Why do people read negative Internet comments and do other things that will obviously be painful? Because humans have an inherent need to 1 uncertainty, according to a recent study in Psychological Science. The new research reveals that the need to know is so strong that people will 2 to satisfy their curiosity even when it is clear the answer will 3.
paras.zh: 人们为什么会去读互联网上的负面评论，还会做其他显然会让自己痛苦的事情？一项发表于《心理科学》的新近研究认为，这是因为人类天生有一种消除不确定性的需求。这项新研究表明，想知道答案的需求如此强烈，以至于即使答案明显会令人痛苦，人们也会设法满足自己的好奇心。

paras.en: In a series of four experiments, behavioral scientists at the University of Chicago and the Wisconsin School of Business tested students' willingness to 4 themselves to unpleasant stimuli in an effort to satisfy curiosity. For one 5, each participant was shown a pile of pens that the researcher claimed were from a previous experiment. The twist? Half of the pens would 6 an electric shock when clicked.
paras.zh: 在一系列四项实验中，芝加哥大学与威斯康星商学院的行为科学家测试了学生为满足好奇心而让自己接触不快刺激的意愿。以其中一次试验为例：每位参与者面前摆着一堆笔，研究者称这些笔来自此前的一次实验。转折在哪里？其中一半的笔在按下时会放出电击。

paras.en: Twenty-seven students were told which pens were electrified; another twenty-seven were told only that some were electrified. 7 left alone in the room, the students who did not know which ones would shock them clicked more pens and incurred more shocks than the students who knew what would 8 . Subsequent experiments reproduced this effect with other stimuli, 9 the sound of fingernails on a chalkboard and photographs of disgusting insects.
paras.zh: 27 名学生被告知哪些笔通了电，另外 27 名学生只被告知其中有些笔通了电。当被单独留在房间里时，不知道哪些笔会电人的学生按下的笔更多，遭到的电击也更多——比起那些知道会发生什么的学生。后续实验用其他刺激再现了这一效应，例如指甲刮黑板的声音和令人作呕的昆虫照片。

paras.en: The drive to 10 is deeply rooted in humans, much the same as the basic drives for 11 or shelter, says Christopher Hsee of the University of Chicago. Curiosity is often considered a good instinct - it can 12 new scientific advances, for instance - but sometimes such 13 can backfire. The insight that curiosity can drive you to do 14 things is a profound one.
paras.zh: 芝加哥大学的克里斯托弗·奚（Christopher Hsee）说，探索的驱动力深深扎根于人类，与对食物或住所的基本需求十分相似。好奇心常被视为一种良好的本能——例如它能够带来新的科学进步——但有时这种探究也会适得其反。"好奇心会驱使你做出自我伤害的事情"这一洞见极为深刻。

paras.en: Unhealthy curiosity is possible to 15, however. In a final experiment, participants who were encouraged to 16 how they would feel after viewing an unpleasant picture were less likely to 17 to see such an image. These results suggest that imagining the 18 of following through on one's curiosity ahead of time can help determine 19 it is worth the endeavor. "Thinking about long-term 20 is key to reducing the possible negative effects of curiosity," Hsee says. In other words, don't read online comments.
paras.zh: "不健康的好奇心"却是可以抵制的。在最后一项实验中，被鼓励去预测自己看完一张不快图片后会有何感受的参与者，选择去看这类图片的可能性更低。这些结果表明，事先设想追随好奇心的结果，有助于判断它是否值得一试。奚说："思考长期后果，是减少好奇心可能带来的负面影响的关键。"换句话说，别去读网上的评论。

items.exp: 定位第二句 Because humans have an inherent need to ___ uncertainty。下文 the need to know 是本空的原词复现，能"消除"不确定性的只有 resolve（resolve uncertainty 为固定搭配）。protect（保护）、ignore（忽视）与"想知道"完全相反，discuss（讨论）不能与 uncertainty 搭配。
空格前是 the need to know is so strong that people will ___ to satisfy their curiosity：为了满足好奇心，人们会"设法、力图"去做，seek to do sth 意为"试图做某事"。refuse 与语义相反，wait to do 强调"等着做"，regret to do 意为"遗憾地要去做"，均不合。
even when 引导让步，暗示"答案对自己不利也照看不误"。首句 obviously be painful 与 negative 已给出情感基调，故 the answer will hurt（答案会伤人）。last（持续）、rise（上升）与"答案"不搭，mislead（误导）与本段"痛苦"的语义线索无关。

tested students' willingness to ___ themselves to unpleasant stimuli：expose oneself to sth 意为"使自己接触到（不利的事物）"，与 unpleasant stimuli 搭配恰到好处。alert sb to sth 是"提醒某人注意"，tie...to 是"把……绑到"，treat sb to sth 是"招待"，都不能与反身代词加 unpleasant stimuli 连用。
For one ___ 引出四项实验中的"其中一项"，trial 意为"试验"，与前文 a series of four experiments 对应。message（信息）、review（评论）、concept（概念）都不能表示"一次试验"。
Half of the pens would ___ an electric shock when clicked：deliver an electric shock 是"放出电击"的固定搭配。remove（移除）、weaken（减弱）、interrupt（打断）都不能以 electric shock 为宾语。
___ left alone in the room 是分词短语作状语，逻辑主语为后面的 the students，表示"当被单独留在房间里时"，用 When。若填 If，则变成"如果被留下"，与实验事实不符；Though 表让步、Unless 表否定条件，均不通。
than the students who knew what would ___：与前面 did not know which ones would shock them 对照，知道的是"会发生什么"，故 happen。continue（继续）、disappear（消失）、change（改变）都无法概括"哪支笔会放电"这件事。
空格后 the sound of fingernails on a chalkboard and photographs of disgusting insects 是对 other stimuli 的举例，故 such as。rather than 表取舍、regardless of 表不顾、owing to 表原因，逻辑都不对。
The drive to ___ is deeply rooted in humans：本句把这种驱动力与对食物、住所的基本需求并列，回指上文的 curiosity、the need to know，即"探索、发现"的驱动力，故 discover。forgive、forget、disagree 与"求知"无关。
the basic drives for ___ or shelter：与 shelter（住所）并列的只能是维持生存的基本需求，food or shelter 是常见搭配。pay、marriage、schooling 都不属于"基本生存需求"。
it can ___ new scientific advances 中的 it 指 curiosity，好奇心能够"带来"新的科学进步，故 lead to。rest on（依赖于）、learn from（向……学习）、begin with（以……开始）都会把因果说反。
such ___ 指代前半句的好奇心、探究，inquiry（探究、询问）与之同义复现，且能与 backfire（适得其反）搭配。withdrawal（退缩）、persistence（坚持）、diligence（勤奋）都不是"好奇心"的同义表达。
curiosity can drive you to do ___ things：上文反复强调 painful、negative、backfire，说明好奇心会让人做"自我伤害"的事，故 self-destructive。self-reliant（自立的）、self-evident（不言而喻的）、self-deceptive（自欺的）都不承接"痛苦"这条线索。
Unhealthy curiosity is possible to ___, however：however 表转折，上文说好奇心会伤到自己，这里转说"不健康的好奇心是可以抵制的"，且下文"被鼓励预测感受的人更少去看图片"正是抵制的例证，故 resist。define、replace、trace 与下文的实验逻辑接不上。
encouraged to ___ how they would feel after viewing an unpleasant picture：让被试预先"预测"自己的感受，与末段 imagining... ahead of time 呼应，故 predict。overlook（忽视）、conceal（隐藏）与"设想感受"相反，design 不搭配 how they would feel。
were less likely to ___ to see such an image：be likely to do 后接"选择去看"，choose to see 意为"选择去看"。remember to see、pretend to see 语义不通，promise to see 也不合"意愿"这一主题。
imagining the ___ of following through on one's curiosity：设想"把好奇心付诸行动的结果"，outcome 与后文 whether it is worth the endeavor（是否值得一试）直接对应。relief（宽慰）、plan（计划）、duty（责任）都不能与 following through 构成"结果"关系。
can help determine ___ it is worth the endeavor：determine 后接 whether 引导的宾语从句，意为"判断是否值得一试"。why、where、how 都无法与 worth 构成"值不值得"的判断。
Thinking about long-term ___ is key to reducing the possible negative effects：与 negative effects 同义复现的是"长期后果"，故 consequences。investments、strategies、limitations 都不能解释"为什么能减少负面影响"。

sections.title: Text 1　职业教育与实践教育
sections.dir: Read the text and answer the questions by choosing A, B, C or D.
sections.note: 主题：一所技术高中为何值得被肯定。作者先立靶（偏见）再破靶（数据）。

paras.en: It is curious that Stephen Koziatek feels almost as though he has to justify his efforts to give his students a better future.
paras.zh: 斯蒂芬·科齐亚泰克（Stephen Koziatek）几乎觉得自己必须为"给学生一个更好的未来"所做的努力辩护，这一点颇令人费解。

paras.en: Mr. Koziatek is part of something pioneering. He is a teacher at a New Hampshire high school where learning is not something of books and tests and mechanical memorization, but practical. When did it become accepted wisdom that students should be able to name the 13th president of the United States but be utterly overwhelmed by a broken bike chain?
paras.zh: 科齐亚泰克先生参与的是一件具有开创性的事。他在新罕布什尔州一所高中任教，那里所学的不是书本、考试和机械记忆，而是实用的东西。从什么时候起，"学生能说出美国第 13 任总统的名字，却被一根断掉的车链难住"竟成了公认的常识？

paras.en: As Koziatek knows, there is learning in just about everything. Nothing is necessarily gained by forcing students to learn geometry at a graffiti-covered desk stuck with generations of discarded chewing gum. They can also learn geometry by assembling a bicycle.
paras.zh: 正如科齐亚泰克所知，几乎万事之中皆有学问。硬要学生趴在一张沾满一代代人口香糖残渣的涂鸦课桌上学习几何，未必能带来什么收获。他们同样可以通过组装一辆自行车来学几何。

paras.en: But he's also found a kind of insidious prejudice. Working with your hands is seen as almost a mark of inferiority. Schools in the family of vocational education "have that stereotype… that it's for kids who can't make it academically," he says.
paras.zh: 但他也发现了一种隐蔽的偏见：动手做事几乎被视为低人一等的标志。他在提到职业教育时说，这类学校"总带着那种刻板印象——它是给学业上不行的孩子准备的"。

paras.en: On one hand, that viewpoint is a logical product of America's evolution. Manufacturing is not the economic engine that it once was. The job security that the US economy once offered to high school graduates has largely evaporated. More education is the new principle. We want more for our kids, and rightfully so.
paras.zh: 一方面，这种看法是美国发展演变的合乎逻辑的产物。制造业已不再是昔日的经济引擎。美国经济曾经给予高中毕业生的那份工作保障，如今已基本消失。受更多教育成了新的准则。我们希望孩子得到更多，这完全正当。

paras.en: But the headlong push into bachelor's degrees for all — and the subtle devaluing of anything less — misses an important point: That's not the only thing the American economy needs. Yes, a bachelor's degree opens more doors. But even now, 54 percent of the jobs in the country are middle-skill jobs, such as construction and high-skill manufacturing. But only 44 percent of workers are adequately trained.
paras.zh: 但一窝蜂地推动"人人都读本科"——并悄悄贬低其他一切——忽略了一个要点：这并非美国经济唯一需要的东西。是的，本科学位能打开更多的门。但即便在当下，全国 54% 的岗位仍是中等技能岗位，比如建筑和高技能制造业。而只有 44% 的劳动者受过足够的训练。

paras.en: In other words, at a time when the working class has turned the country on its political head, frustrated that the opportunity that once defined America is vanishing, one obvious solution is staring us in the face. There is a gap in working-class jobs, but the workers who need those jobs most aren't equipped to do them. Koziatek's Manchester School of Technology High School is trying to fill that gap.
paras.zh: 换句话说，在工人阶级把这个国家的政治格局彻底掀翻、并为自己曾经定义美国的那个机会正在消失而愤懑之时，一个显而易见的解决办法就摆在眼前：蓝领岗位存在缺口，而最需要这些岗位的工人却没有能力胜任。科齐亚泰克的曼彻斯特技术高中正试图填补这个缺口。

paras.en: Koziatek's school is a wake-up call. When education becomes one-size-fits-all, it risks overlooking a nation's diversity of gifts.
paras.zh: 科齐亚泰克的学校是一记警钟。当教育变成一刀切，它就有可能忽视一个国家天赋的多样性。

items.stem: A broken bike chain is mentioned to show students' lack of
items.exp: 定位第二段末句：学生能说出第 13 任总统是谁，却被一根断掉的车链难住。作者用这个对比说明学校教育重书本、轻动手，学生缺的是"实践能力"，故选 A。B 恰恰是他们富余的东西；C 是科齐亚泰克所做的事，与"学生缺少"无关；D 是他们被训练的能力，方向相反。

items.stem: There exists the prejudice that vocational education is for kids who
items.exp: 定位第四段引语：it's for kids who can't make it academically，即"学业上不成功"的孩子，与 C 同义。A 把 stereotype 从"对职业教育的看法"错移到"孩子思维僵化"；B、D 文中均无依据。

items.stem: We can infer from Paragraph 5 that high school graduates
opts: used to have big financial concerns
used to have more job opportunities
are reluctant to work in manufacturing
are entitled to more educational privileges
items.exp: 第五段说 The job security that the US economy once offered to high school graduates has largely evaporated（曾提供给高中毕业生的工作保障已基本消失）。"保障消失"反推"过去机会更多"，故 B。A 的 financial concerns 文中未提；C、D 属无中生有。

items.stem: The headlong push into bachelor's degrees for all
opts: helps create a lot of middle-skill jobs
may narrow the gap in working-class jobs
is expected to yield a better-trained workforce
indicates the overvaluing of higher education
items.exp: 第六段说这种推动伴随着 the subtle devaluing of anything less（对本科以下学历的悄然贬低），把本科学位抬得高于其他一切，即"高估高等教育"，故 D。A、B 与文意相反：正是这种推动忽视了 54% 的中等技能岗位缺口；C 与 only 44% of workers are adequately trained 矛盾。

items.stem: The author's attitude toward Koziatek's school can be described as
items.exp: 末段称这所学校是 a wake-up call（一记警钟），并批评一刀切教育会忽视天赋多样性，字里行间都在肯定科齐亚泰克的做法，故为"支持"。tolerant（容忍）语气过弱，disappointed、cautious 与作者立场相反。

sections.title: Text 2　可再生能源的拐点
sections.dir: Read the text and answer the questions by choosing A, B, C or D.
sections.note: 主题：可再生能源正在取代化石燃料。注意"趋势"与"现状"的区别，选项常在这里设坑。

paras.en: While fossil fuels - coal, oil, gas - still generate roughly 85 percent of the world's energy supply, it's clearer than ever that the future belongs to renewable sources such as wind and solar. The move to renewables is picking up momentum around the world: They now account for more than half of new power sources going on line.
paras.zh: 尽管化石燃料——煤、石油、天然气——仍提供全球约 85% 的能源，但未来属于风能、太阳能等可再生能源这一点，比以往任何时候都更清楚。向可再生能源的转变正在世界各地积聚势头：在新投产的电源中，它们已占一半以上。

paras.en: Some growth stems from a commitment by governments and farsighted businesses to fund cleaner energy sources. But increasingly the story is about the plummeting prices of renewables, especially wind and solar. The cost of solar panels has dropped by 80 percent and the cost of wind turbines by close to one-third in the past eight years.
paras.zh: 部分增长源于各国政府和有远见的企业对寻找更清洁能源的承诺。但越来越多的故事，讲的是可再生能源价格的暴跌，尤其是风电和光伏。过去八年，太阳能电池板成本下降了 80%，风机成本下降了近三分之一。

paras.en: In many parts of the world renewable energy is already a principal energy source. In Scotland, for example, wind turbines provide enough electricity to power 95 percent of homes. While the rest of the world takes the lead, notably China and Europe, the United States is also seeing a remarkable shift. In March, for the first time, wind and solar power accounted for more than 10 percent of the power generated in the US, reported the US Energy Information Administration.
paras.zh: 在世界许多地方，可再生能源已是主要能源。以苏格兰为例，风机提供的电力足以满足 95% 家庭的用电。在世界其他地区（尤其是中国和欧洲）领先的同时，美国也正经历显著转变。美国能源信息署报告称，今年 3 月，风电和光伏发电量首次占美国总发电量的 10% 以上。

paras.en: President Trump has underlined fossil fuels — especially coal — as the path to economic growth. In a recent speech in Iowa, he dismissed wind power as an unreliable energy source. But that message did not play well with many in Iowa, where wind turbines dot the fields and provide 36 percent of the state's electricity generation - and where tech giants like Microsoft are being attracted by the availability of clean energy to power their data centers.
paras.zh: 特朗普总统强调化石燃料——尤其是煤——是经济增长之路。在爱荷华州最近的一次演讲中，他把风电斥为不可靠的能源。但这一说法在爱荷华州的许多人那里并不受欢迎：那里风机点缀田野，提供了全州 36% 的发电量；微软等科技巨头也正被清洁能源的可得性吸引，来为它们的数据中心供电。

paras.en: The question "what happens when the wind doesn't blow or the sun doesn't shine?" has provided a quick put-down for skeptics. But a boost in the storage capacity of batteries is making their ability to keep power flowing around the clock more likely.
paras.zh: "风不吹、太阳不晒的时候怎么办？"这个问题一直是对怀疑论者的现成回击。但电池储能容量的提升，正让"全天候持续供电"变得更有可能。

paras.en: The advance is driven in part by vehicle manufacturers, who are placing big bets on battery-powered electric vehicles. Although electric cars are still a rarity on roads now, this massive investment could change the picture rapidly in coming years.
paras.zh: 这一进步部分由汽车制造商推动，它们正把重注押在电池驱动的电动汽车上。尽管电动车如今在道路上仍属少见，但这笔巨额投资可能在今后几年迅速改变局面。

paras.en: While there's a long way to go, the trend lines for renewables are spiking. The pace of change in energy sources appears to be speeding up — perhaps just in time to have a meaningful effect in slowing climate change. What Washington does — or doesn't do — to promote alternative energy may mean less and less at a time of a global shift in thought.
paras.zh: 尽管还有很长的路要走，可再生能源的趋势线正在陡升。能源更替的步伐似乎在加快——或许恰好及时，能在减缓气候变化上产生实质影响。在全球思想转变之际，华盛顿做什么、或不做什么，或许越来越不重要了。

items.stem: The word "Plummeting" (Line 3, Para. 2) is closest in meaning to
items.exp: 定位第二段：the plummeting prices of renewables，紧接着用数字佐证——太阳能板成本下降 80%、风机成本下降近三分之一。价格"大幅下降"即 falling。stabilizing（趋稳）、rising（上升）与数字矛盾，changing 过于笼统。

items.stem: According to Paragraph 3, the use of renewable energy in America
opts: is as extensive as in Europe
items.exp: 第三段说 the United States is also seeing a remarkable shift，并给出"风光发电首超 10%"的数据，remarkable shift 即"进展显著"，故 A。B 与 While the rest of the world takes the lead, notably China and Europe 矛盾——美国是追赶者；C、D 文中未提，且与"显著转变"相反。

items.stem: It can be learned that in Iowa
opts: wind is a widely used energy source
wind energy has replaced fossil fuels
tech giants are investing in clean energy
there is a shortage of clean energy supply
items.exp: 第四段：爱荷华州 wind turbines dot the fields and provide 36 percent of the state's electricity，风机遍布田野、贡献 36% 电力，说明风电被广泛使用，故 A。B 的 replaced 过度——36% 不等于取代化石燃料；C 把"被清洁能源吸引来供电"夸大为"投资清洁能源"；D 与"供电充足"相反。

items.stem: Which of the following is true about clean energy according to Paragraphs 5&6?
opts: Its application has boosted battery storage.
It is commonly used in car manufacturing.
Its continuous supply is becoming a reality.
Its sustainable exploitation will remain difficult.
items.exp: 第五段末：a boost in the storage capacity of batteries is making their ability to keep power flowing around the clock more likely——储能提升让"全天候持续供电"更可能，故 C。A 因果颠倒，是储能提升推动清洁能源应用，而非相反；B 把"车企投资电动车"说成"造车普遍使用清洁能源"；D 与文意相反。

items.stem: It can be inferred from the last Paragraph that renewable energy
opts: will bring the US closer to other countries
is not really encouraged by the US government
is not competitive enough with regard to its cost
items.exp: 末段：What Washington does — or doesn't do — to promote alternative energy may mean less and less，联邦政府的态度"越来越不重要"，反衬出它并未真正鼓励可再生能源（呼应第四段特朗普贬低风电），故 C。A、B 无据；D 与"成本大幅下降"相反。

sections.title: Text 3　数字巨头与我们的数据
sections.dir: Read the text and answer the questions by choosing A, B, C or D.
sections.note: 主题：巨头真正卖的是数据。难点是"用户不是客户"这一句，34 题就考它。

paras.en: The power and ambition of the giants of the digital economy is astonishing- Amazon has just announced the purchase of the upmarket grocery chain Whole Foods for $ 13.5bn, but two years ago Facebook paid even more than that to acquire the WhatsApp messaging service, which doesn't have any physical product at all. What WhatsApp offered Facebook was an intricate and finely detailed web of its users' friendships and social lives.
paras.zh: 数字经济巨头们的实力与野心令人震惊——亚马逊刚刚宣布以 135 亿美元收购高端连锁超市全食（Whole Foods），而两年前 Facebook 为收购 WhatsApp 即时通讯服务付出的代价更高，可后者根本没有任何实体产品。WhatsApp 给 Facebook 的，是一张由用户友谊与社交生活织成的、错综精细的网络。

paras.en: Facebook promised the European commission then that it would not link phone numbers to Facebook identities, but it broke the promise almost as soon as the deal went through. Even without knowing what was in the messages, the knowledge of who sent them and to whom was enormously revealing and still could be. What political journalist, what party whip, would not want to know the makeup of the WhatsApp groups in which Theresa May's enemies are currently plotting? It may be that the value of Whole Foods to Amazon is not so much the 460 shops it owns, but the records of which customers have purchased what.
paras.zh: Facebook 当时向欧盟委员会承诺，不会把电话号码与 Facebook 身份关联，但交易一完成它就几乎立刻违背了承诺。即使不知道消息内容，"谁发给了谁"这一信息本身就极具揭示性，而且今后仍可能如此。哪位政治记者、哪位党鞭，会不想知道特雷莎·梅的对手们正在其中谋划的 WhatsApp 群组都由谁组成？也许全食对亚马逊的价值，与其说是它拥有的 460 家门店，不如说是"哪位顾客买过什么"的记录。

paras.en: Competition law appears to be the only way to address these imbalances of power. But it is clumsy. For one thing, it is very slow compared to the pace of change within the digital economy. By the time a problem has been addressed and remedied it may have vanished in the marketplace, to be replaced by new abuses of power. But there is a deeper conceptual problem, too.
paras.zh: 竞争法似乎是纠正这些权力失衡的唯一途径。但它很笨拙。其一，与数字经济内部的变革速度相比，它太慢了：等问题被受理并补救，它可能已从市场上消失，被新的权力滥用所取代。其二还有一个更深层的概念问题。

paras.en: Competition law as presently interpreted deals with financial disadvantage to consumers and this is not obvious when the users of these services don't pay for them. The users of their services are not their customers. That would be the people who buy advertising from them - and Facebook and Google, the two virtual giants, dominate digital advertising to the disadvantage of all other media and entertainment companies.
paras.zh: 按现行解释，竞争法处理的是消费者遭受的经济损失，而这些服务的用户并不付费，这种损失就不明显了。这些服务的使用者并不是它们的客户——客户是那些向它们购买广告的人。而 Facebook 与谷歌这两大虚拟巨头，正支配着数字广告，使其他所有媒体与娱乐公司处于不利地位。

paras.en: The product they're selling is data, and we, the users, convert our lives to data for the benefit of the digital giants. Just as some ants farm the bugs called aphids for the honeydew they produce when they feed, so Google farms us for the data that our digital lives yield. Ants keep predatory insects away from where their aphids feed; Gmail keeps the spammers out of our inboxes. It doesn't feel like a human or democratic relationship, even if both sides benefit.
paras.zh: 它们出售的产品是数据，而我们这些用户把自己的生活转化为数据，供数字巨头获利。就像有些蚂蚁饲养蚜虫，取食它们进食时分泌的蜜露一样，谷歌"饲养"我们，为的是我们的数字生活所产生的数据。蚂蚁把捕食性昆虫挡在蚜虫觅食地之外；Gmail 则把垃圾邮件挡在我们的收件箱之外。这不像是一种人与人、或民主的关系，即便双方都获益。

items.stem: According to Paragraph 1, Facebook acquired WhatsApp for its
items.exp: 首段末句：WhatsApp 提供的是 an intricate and finely detailed web of its users' friendships and social lives，即用户的社交关系信息。再看第二段"谁发给了谁"极具揭示性，进一步说明 Facebook 要的是用户信息，故 B。A、C 与 which doesn't have any physical product at all 直接矛盾；D 文中未提。

items.stem: Linking phone numbers to Facebook identities may
opts: pose a risk to Facebook users
items.exp: 第二段：绑定手机号与身份后，"谁发给谁"的信息极具揭示性，还可能被政治记者、党鞭利用来窥探群组构成——这暴露的是普通用户的隐私风险，故 C。A 把"被政治人物利用"说成"加剧政治争端"；B 张冠李戴（客户记录是全食的例子）；D 是违背承诺，不是"误导委员会"。

items.stem: According to the author, competition law
opts: should serve the new market powers
should not provide just one legal solution
cannot keep pace with the changing market
items.exp: 第三段：it is very slow compared to the pace of change within the digital economy；等问题处理完，它可能已经从市场上消失。即竞争法跟不上市场变化，故 D。A 与"纠正权力失衡"相反；B 文中未说竞争法会加剧失衡；C 是对"深层概念问题"的误读。

items.stem: Competition law as presently interpreted can hardly protect Facebook users because
opts: they are not defined as customers
the services are paid for by advertisers
items.exp: 第四段：竞争法处理的是"消费者的经济损失"，但这些服务的使用者不付费，The users of their services are not their customers——用户不被视为客户，因而落在保护范围之外，故 A。D 是 A 成立的原因，但题目问的是"保护不到"的直接理由；B、C 文中无据。

items.stem: The ants analogy is used to illustrate
opts: a win-win business model between digital giants
a typical competition pattern among digital giants
the benefits provided for digital giants' customers
the relationship between digital giants and their users
items.exp: 末段：蚂蚁饲养蚜虫取蜜露，正如谷歌"饲养"我们以获取数据；蚂蚁驱赶蚜虫的天敌，正如 Gmail 拦截垃圾邮件。这个类比说明的是巨头与用户之间"看似互惠、实则不对等"的关系，故 D。A 忽略了末句 It doesn't feel like a human or democratic relationship；B、C 均偏离类比的落点。

sections.title: Text 4　深度工作与“偷懒”
sections.dir: Read the text and answer the questions by choosing A, B, C or D.
sections.note: 主题：少做一点反而做得更多。全文是"方法罗列"，主旨题（40）选覆盖面最大的那个。

paras.en: To combat the trap of putting a premium on being busy, Cal Newport, author of Deep Work: Rules for Focused Success in a Distracted World, recommends building a habit of "deep work" - the ability to focus without distraction.
paras.zh: 为了跳出"以忙碌为荣"的陷阱，《深度工作：在纷扰世界中专注成功的法则》一书作者卡尔·纽波特建议养成"深度工作"的习惯——即不受干扰地专注的能力。

paras.en: There are a number of approaches to mastering the art of deep work - be it lengthy retreats dedicated to a specific task; developing a daily ritual; or taking a "journalistic" approach to seizing moments of deep work when you can throughout the day. Whichever approach, the key is to determine your length of focus time and stick to it.
paras.zh: 掌握深度工作这门艺术有多种途径：可以是为某项特定任务而进行的长时段闭关；可以建立每日例行的仪式；也可以采取"记者式"的做法，在全天随时抓住可以深度工作的时刻。无论哪种途径，关键在于确定自己的专注时长，并坚持执行。

paras.en: Newport also recommends "deep scheduling" to combat constant interruptions and get more done in less time. "At any given point, I should have deep work scheduled for roughly the next month. Once on the calendar, I protect this time like I would a doctor's appointment or important meeting", he writes.
paras.zh: 纽波特还建议"深度排期"，以对抗不断的打扰，用更少的时间完成更多的事。他写道："在任何时点，我都应当已为下个月大致排好深度工作。一旦上了日程，我就保护这段时间，如同保护与医生的预约或重要会议。"

paras.en: Another approach to getting more done in less time is to rethink how you prioritise your day - in particular how we craft our to-do lists. Tim Harford, author of Messy: The Power of Disorder to Transform Our Lives, points to a study in the early 1980s that divided undergraduates into two groups: some were advised to set out monthly goals and study activities; others were told to plan activities and goals in much more detail, day by day.
paras.zh: 另一种用更少时间完成更多事的方法，是重新思考如何安排一天的轻重缓急——特别是如何拟定待办清单。《混乱：改变我们生活的无序之力》作者蒂姆·哈福德提到 20 世纪 80 年代初的一项研究：研究者把本科生分成两组，一组被建议制定月度目标和学习活动，另一组则被要求把活动和目标规划得细致得多，具体到每一天。

paras.en: While the researchers assumed that the well-structured daily plans would be most effective when it came to the execution of tasks, they were wrong: the detailed daily plans demotivated students. Harford argues that inevitable distractions often render the daily to-do list ineffective, while leaving room for improvisation in such a list can reap the best results.
paras.zh: 研究者原本以为，结构良好的每日计划在执行任务时最有效，但他们错了：详细的每日计划反而让学生失去动力。哈福德认为，不可避免的干扰常使每日待办清单失效，而在清单中留出即兴发挥的余地，反而能取得最佳效果。

paras.en: In order to make the most of our focus and energy, we also need to embrace downtime, or as Newport suggests, "be lazy".
paras.zh: 为了最大限度地利用我们的专注与精力，我们还需要拥抱"停工期"，或者如纽波特所说，"懒一点"。

paras.en: "Idleness is not just a vacation, an indulgence or a vice; it is as indispensable to the brain as vitamin D is to the body… [idleness] is, paradoxically, necessary to getting any work done," he argues.
paras.zh: 他论证道："闲散不只是休假、放纵或恶习；它对大脑的作用，正如维生素 D 对身体的作用一样不可或缺……矛盾的是，闲散恰恰是完成任何工作的必要条件。"

paras.en: Srini Pillay, an assistant professor of psychiatry at Harvard Medical School, believes this counterintuitive link between downtime and productivity may be due to the way our brains operate. When our brains switch between being focused and unfocused on a task, they tend to be more efficient.
paras.zh: 哈佛医学院精神病学助理教授斯里尼·皮莱认为，停工期与生产力之间这种反直觉的联系，可能源于我们大脑的运作方式：当大脑在专注于某项任务与不专注之间切换时，往往效率更高。

paras.en: "What people don't realise is that in order to complete these tasks they need to use both the focus and unfocus circuits in their brain," says Pillay.
paras.zh: 皮莱说："人们没有意识到的是，要完成这些任务，他们需要同时动用大脑中的专注回路和不专注回路。"

items.stem: The key to mastering the art of deep work is to
items.exp: 第二段末句直接给出答案：the key is to determine your length of focus time and stick to it——确定专注时长并坚持，故 A（keep to 即 stick to）。B、C 是后文待办清单与每日计划的内容，且被证明效果不佳；D 与"不被打扰地专注"相悖。

items.stem: The study in the early 1980s cited by Harford shows that
opts: daily schedules are indispensable to studying
students are hardly motivated by monthly goals
detailed plans may not be as fruitful as expected
items.exp: 第五段：研究者本以为详细计划最有效，"但他们错了"，详细计划反而让学生失去动力。故 D（详细计划未必如预期那样有效）。A 把"留出即兴余地"夸大为"干扰提高效率"；B 与结论相反；C 文中未比较月度目标的效果。

items.stem: According to Newport, idleness is
opts: a desirable mental state for busy people
a major contributor to physical health
an effective way to save time and energy
an essential factor in accomplishing any work
items.exp: 第七段引纽波特：闲散对大脑的作用如维生素 D 对身体，"necessary to getting any work done"——是完成任何工作的必要条件，故 D。A 太笼统且非纽波特原意；B 把"对大脑"偷换成"对身体健康"；C 文中未说闲散能"省时省力"。

items.stem: Pillay believes that our brains' shift between being focused and unfocused
opts: is aimed at better balance in work
items.exp: 第八段末：When our brains switch between being focused and unfocused on a task, they tend to be more efficient，即这种切换能带来更高效率，故 B。A 的 well-being、C 的 balance、D 的 urgency 均无原文支撑。

items.stem: This text is mainly about
opts: ways to relieve the tension of busy life
approaches to getting more done in less time
the cause of the lack of focus time
items.exp: 全文围绕"如何用更少时间做更多事"展开：深度工作、深度排期、待办清单、拥抱停工期，都是 approaches，故 B。A 的"缓解紧张"、C 的"消除干扰"、D 的"缺乏专注时间的原因"都只覆盖某个细节，不能统摄全文。

sections.title: Section II Part B　选小标题
sections.dir: Choose the most suitable subtitle from the list A–G for each numbered paragraph (41–45). Two extra subtitles are not needed.
sections.note: 先划出 A–G 的关键动作词，再读段落找"同义动作"。两个多余项一定是"擦边但方向不对"。
sections.intro: Five ways to make conversation with anyone Conversations are links, which means when you have a conversation with a new person a link gets formed and every conversation you have after that moment will strengthen the link. You meet new people every day: the grocery worker, the cab driver, new people at work or the security guard at the door. Simply starting a conversation with them will form a link. Here are five simple ways that you can make the first move and start a conversation with strangers.
sections.tail: That's it. Five amazing ways that you can make conversation with almost anyone. Every person is a really good book to read, or to have a conversation with!

blocks.en: Suppose you are in a room with someone you don't know and something within you says "I want to talk with this person" — this is something that mostly happens with all of us. You wanted to say something — the first word — but it just won't come out, it feels like it is stuck somewhere. I know the feeling and here is my advice: just get it out. Just think: what is the worst that could happen? They won't talk with you? Well, they are not talking with you now! I truly believe that once you get that first word out everything else will just flow. So keep it simple: "Hi", "Hey"or "Hello" — do the best you can to gather all of the enthusiasm and energy you can, put on a big smile and say "Hi".
blocks.zh: 假设你和一个不认识的人同处一室，内心有个声音说"我想和这个人聊聊"——这几乎是我们所有人都会遇到的事。你想说点什么，想说第一个词，可它就是出不来，仿佛卡在了某处。我懂这种感觉，我的建议是：把它说出来就好。想一想：最坏能怎样？他们不跟你说话？可他们现在也没在跟你说话呀！我真心相信，只要第一个词说出口，其余的一切都会自然流淌。所以保持简单："嗨""嘿"或者"你好"——尽力把热情和能量聚起来，绽开一个大大的笑容，说声"嗨"。
blocks.exp: 本段反复出现 the first word、just get it out、say "Hi"，核心动作是"把话说出口"，对应 A Just say it。C 的 compliment（赞美）文中只字未提，是典型的"看似相关"干扰项。

blocks.en: It is a problem all of us face; you have limited time with the person that you want to talk with and you want to make this talk memorable. Honestly, if we got stuck in the rut of "hi", "hello", "how are you?" and ''what is going on?", you will fail to give the initial jolt to the conversation that can make it so memorable. So don't be afraid to ask more personal questions. Trust me, you'll be surprised to see how much people are willing to share if you just ask.
blocks.zh: 这是我们所有人都面临的问题：你和想交谈的人只有有限的时间，而你想让这次谈话令人难忘。说实话，如果我们陷在"嗨""你好""最近怎么样""在忙什么"的老套里，就无法给对话最初的那一推，让它变得难忘。所以别怕问更私人的问题。相信我，你会惊讶地发现，只要你问，人们多么愿意分享。
blocks.exp: 本段明确反对 if we got stuck in the rut of "hi", "hello", "how are you?"，主张 don't be afraid to ask more personal questions，即跳过寒暄、直接深入，对应 F Skip the small talk。A 只讲"开口"，而本段已假设你会开口。

blocks.en: When you meet a person for the first time, make an effort to find the things which you and that person have in common so that you can build the conversation from that point. When you start conversation from there and then move outwards, you'll find all of a sudden that the conversation becomes a lot easier.
blocks.zh: 第一次见到某人时，努力找出你和对方的共同点，这样你就能从这一点出发构建对话。从这里开始、再向外延伸，你会突然发现对话变得容易多了。
blocks.exp: 本段的关键词是 find the things which you and that person have in common、build the conversation from that point，即寻找共同点，对应 E Find the "me too"s。G 的 ask for an opinion 是"征求意见"，与"找共同点"不是一回事。

blocks.en: Imagine you are pouring your heart out to someone and they are just busy on their phone, and if you ask for their attention you get the response "I can multitask". So when someone tries to communicate with you, just be in that communication wholeheartedly. Make eye contact. Trust me, eye contact is where all the magic happens. When you make eye contact, you can feel the conversation.
blocks.zh: 想象你正对某人倾诉心声，对方却忙着看手机，你请求他注意，得到的回答是"我可以一心多用"。所以，当有人试图与你交流时，就全心全意地投入这次交流。要有眼神接触。相信我，眼神接触是奇迹发生之处。当你与对方有眼神交流时，你能"感受到"这场对话。
blocks.exp: 本段要求 be in that communication wholeheartedly、make eye contact，讲的是"人在场、心也在场"，对应 B Be present。D 的 name/places/things 是下一段的内容，注意不要串段。

blocks.en: You all came into a conversation where you first met the person, but after some time you may have met again and have forgotten their name. Isn't that awkward! So, remember the little details of the people you met or you talked with; perhaps the places they have been to, the places they want to go, the things they like, the things they hate — whatever you talk about. When you remember such things you can automatically become investor in their wellbeing. So they feel a responsibility to you to keep that relationship going.
blocks.zh: 你们因为初次见面而开始了一段对话，但过了一段时间，你们可能又遇见了，却忘了对方的名字。那多尴尬！所以，记住你见过或交谈过的人的那些小细节：他们去过的地方、想去的地方、喜欢的东西、讨厌的东西——不管你们聊过什么。当你记住这些时，你自然而然就成了他们幸福的"投资者"，于是他们也会觉得有责任把这段关系维系下去。
blocks.exp: 本段说 remember the little details——the places they have been to、the things they like/hate，还提到忘记 their name 的尴尬，正是"名字、地点、物品"，对应 D Name, places, things。

sections.title: Section III　翻译
sections.dir: Translate the following text into Chinese. (15 points)
sections.note: 英译汉按句给分，先切句、再定主谓、最后调语序。被动与分词短语是主要难点。

paras.en: A fifth grader gets a homework assignment to select his future career path from a list of occupations. He ticks "astronaut" but quickly adds "scientist" to the list and selects it as well. The boy is convinced that if he reads enough, he can explore as many career paths as he likes. And so he reads - everything from encyclopedias to science fiction novels. He reads so passionately that his parents have to institute a "no reading policy" at the dinner table.
paras.zh: 一名五年级学生得到一份家庭作业：从一份职业清单中挑选自己未来的职业道路。他勾选了"宇航员"，但很快又在清单上添上"科学家"，并把它也选上了。这个男孩深信，只要书读得足够多，他就能探索任意多条职业道路。于是他开始读书——从百科全书到科幻小说，无所不读。他读得如此痴迷，以致父母不得不在餐桌上定下一条"禁止读书"的规定。

paras.en: That boy was Bill Gates, and he hasn't stopped reading yet - not even after becoming one of the most successful people on the planet. Nowadays, his reading material has changed from science fiction and reference books: recently, he revealed that he reads at least 50 nonfiction books a year. Gates chooses nonfiction titles because they explain how the world works. "Each book opens up new avenues of knowledge to explore", Gates says.
paras.zh: 那个男孩就是比尔·盖茨，而他至今没有停止读书——即使在成为这个星球上最成功的人士之一以后也没有。如今，他的阅读材料已从科幻小说和工具书转向别处：最近他透露，自己一年至少读 50 本非虚构类书籍。盖茨选择非虚构类书籍，是因为它们解释世界如何运转。"每一本书都开辟出可供探索的新知识途径，"盖茨说。

sections.title: Section IV Part A　应用文（道歉信）
sections.dir: Suppose you have to cancel your travel plan and will not be able to visit Professor Smith. Write him an email to 1) apologize and explain the situation, and 2) suggest a future meeting. (about 100 words)
sections.note: 三段式：①说明写信目的并致歉 ②解释原因、表达歉意 ③提出改期建议并致谢。语气要正式，署名 Li Ming。
sections.sample:
Dear Professor Smith,

I am writing to apologize for having to cancel my travel plan and therefore missing our appointment next Friday. An unexpected family emergency requires me to return home immediately, so I am afraid I will not be able to visit you as we arranged.

I feel terribly sorry for any inconvenience this may cause you. Would it be possible for us to meet at your convenience later this month? I will be back in Beijing by the 20th and am free any afternoon that week.

Thank you for your understanding, and I look forward to your reply.

Sincerely yours,
Li Ming
tips: 开头一句点明“道歉 + 取消”，不要绕
原因要具体但简短（family emergency / 突发事务），不必编细节
结尾必须给出补救方案（reschedule），这是题目第 2 点要求，漏了直接扣分

sections.title: Section IV Part B　图表作文
sections.dir: Write an essay based on the chart below. 1) interpret the chart, and 2) give your comments. (about 150 words)
sections.note: 图表：2017 年某市消费者选择餐厅时的关注因素——特色 36.3%、价格 26.8%、环境 23.8%、服务 8.4%、其他 4.7%。
sections.sample:
The pie chart illustrates what consumers in a certain city cared about most when choosing a restaurant in 2017. Specialty tops the list at 36.3%, followed by price (26.8%) and environment (23.8%), while service accounts for only 8.4% and other factors 4.7%.

Two things stand out. First, diners now weigh "what makes this place different" above "how cheap it is": specialty and environment together add up to 60%, far more than price. Second, service, the factor restaurants traditionally advertise, ranks second to last — customers seem to judge a meal by the food and the setting rather than by how attentively they are served.

In my view, this shift reflects a maturing market. As incomes rise, eating out is no longer merely about filling one's stomach but about experience. Restaurants that rely on discounts while neglecting the quality of their dishes will find it hard to keep customers.
tips: 第一段只做“读数”：最大值 + 次大值 + 最小值，不要评论
第二段做“归因/对比”：把特色与环境合并（60%）对抗价格，是最容易被阅卷人记住的写法
第三段给判断：消费升级、体验经济，一句结论即可，不要展开新论点
